ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a diamond-shaped resistor network, with the top vertex as A, the left end as B, the right end as D, and the bottom end as C. The upper-left branch from B to A has an 8 Ω resistor, and the lower-left branch from B to C has a 10 Ω resistor; the upper-right branch from A to D has a 6 Ω resistor; the vertical middle branch from A to C has a 3 Ω resistor; the lower-right branch from D to C is a direct wire, with no resistor. Reasoning: Because D and C are directly connected by a wire, finding R_BD is equivalent to finding the equivalent resistance between B and C. There are two parallel branches between A and C: one is A-D-C, reaching D, which is at the same potential as C, after passing through the 6 Ω resistor; the other is the middle 3 Ω resistor. Therefore, the A-C equivalent resistance is 6 Ω || 3 Ω = (6×3)/(6+3) = 2 Ω. Thus the resistance of the upper path from B through A to C is 8 Ω + 2 Ω = 10 Ω. This 10 Ω path is in parallel with the direct 10 Ω resistor from B to C, so R_BD = R_BC = 10 Ω || 10 Ω = 5 Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology and component values. Since D is directly wired to C, replace D by node C. Between A and C there are two resistors in parallel: 6 Ω on A-D-C and 3 Ω on A-C, giving 2 Ω. The upper-left path from B to C through A is then 8 Ω + 2 Ω = 10 Ω. This is in parallel with the direct B-C 10 Ω resistor, so R_BD = 10 Ω || 10 Ω = 5 Ω.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diamond circuit: terminals/nodes A at top, B at left, C at bottom, D at right; resistors AB = 8 Ω, BC = 10 Ω, AD = 6 Ω, AC = 3 Ω; the branch from D to C is just a wire with no resistor, so D and C are the same electrical node.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to identify that the requested quantity is the equivalent resistance between terminals B and D, reported in ohms.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply ideal-wire node equivalence, then series and parallel resistance rules: resistors sharing the same two nodes are in parallel; resistors carrying the same path current in a branch are in series; parallel formula R_eq = R1 R2/(R1+R2).
